**Where we are ahead:** a deterministic, replayable gate rather than a plotting tool — every guarantee is an invariant with POSITIVE CONTROLS that must fail it (FIFO mix, no cover, an order-preserving release, a blocked mix), run on every test pass; per-mix AND end-to-end metrics against the mix's own law; a direct memorylessness check (`reorderStats`); n−1 detection from loop cover, with a false-positive check (the reference models no active attacks); constant-size mailbox pulls checked; the `sphinx` round trip proving the modeled header stands in for a real onion. **Where we are behind:** the scale a netsim run reaches in a test (160 nodes, `LARGE_CFG`), not thousands of clients, and no peer-to-peer topology with a mix per user (the free route here is a fixed set of mixes).

## Design

Loopix decomposes into two utterly different halves, and this module is built
around that seam:

- **The packet (reused, not built here).** Per-hop unlinkability is Sphinx, and
  `sphinx` already ships it. A Sphinx onion is fixed-length, peels one layer per
  hop, reveals to each hop only its successor + an opaque per-hop payload, and is
  bit-unlinkable across hops. `routing.zig`'s `sphinxRoundTrip` test builds a
  *real* onion for a stratified route with `(next_hop, delay)` in each hop's
  opaque payload and peels it end-to-end — the standing proof the substrate
  works as a mix packet. Reuse caveats (both immaterial to anonymity): `sphinx`
  is secp256k1 + 1366-byte + ≤37-hop (Lightning's parameters, vs Loopix/Nym's
  Curve25519), and Loopix's sender metadata rides inside BOLT#4's opaque payload
  unchanged. The netsim hot loop carries a *modeled* fixed-size header
  (`types.MixHeader`) instead of a real onion, because the anonymity metric is
  purely about timing and the adversary is denied content by construction — the
  modeled header is faithful to the onion's *observable* behaviour (constant
  length, one-mix-per-layer route, per-hop unlinkability).

- **The strategy (the actual subject).** A continuous-time **Poisson mix** (each
  mix holds every arrival an independent exponential delay), **Poisson cover
  traffic**, and a **stratified** topology. This is what makes the whole thing
  unlinkable against a global passive adversary, and it is what this module
  builds, gates, and model-checks.

Layout mirrors the repo's scaffold→gate→positive-control→harness pattern
(`df-elect`, `raft`): `types.zig` (config + header codec), `routing.zig`
(stratified routes + the Sphinx proof), `mixing.zig` (**the mixing core — see
"Mixing core" below**), `adversary.zig` (**the anonymity
invariant + measurement — the real content**), `protocol.zig` (the
`netsim.Protocol` consumers + the FIFO positive control), `gate.zig` (the one
switch, `fable_core_implemented`, `true`).

## Threat model — the anonymity invariant, and how it is measured

**Adversary: a global passive adversary (GPA)** — the standard Loopix/Nym model.
It observes the *timing* of every packet on every link, but (i) cannot read
packet contents (Sphinx layer-encryption makes each hop's bytes unlinkable to
the next — the `id` a `Transit` carries is a harness-only oracle label the
adversary is never handed), and (ii) cannot distinguish real from cover traffic
(chaff is bit-indistinguishable and constant-length — the `kind` label is
likewise withheld). What it CAN do, at each mix `M`, is see the multiset of
arrival times and the multiset of departure times and try to match them: *did
output `d` carry the same packet as input `a`?* That is the anonymity game.

**The metric (`adversary.measure`).** The adversary knows the mix's strategy
(Kerckhoffs), so it links using that strategy's own hold distribution as its
likelihood kernel. For a target that arrived at `M` at `a*`, it assigns each
departure `d` a weight `kernel(d − a*)` (causal: `0` for `d < a*`) and
normalizes to a posterior over "which departure is my target". From that
posterior, two INDEPENDENT quantities are measured, because Loopix's guarantee
has two independent parts:

1. **Effective anonymity set** `2^H`, `H = −Σ pⱼ·log₂ pⱼ` — the Serjantov–Danezis
   metric, the effective number of departures the target could equally be. This
   is what **cover traffic** buys: no chaff ⇒ the pool empties ⇒ the crowd
   shrinks to 1. Measured as a **worst-case min** over all real targets.
2. **Linking probability** `p(d*)` — the posterior mass on the target's TRUE
   departure `d*` (ground truth the harness knows, the adversary does not). This
   is what the **memoryless Poisson hold** buys: a smooth exponential spreads the
   posterior across the in-flight pool, so no single departure concentrates
   mass. Measured as a **worst-case max** over all real targets.

**The invariant (`AnonymityBound`)** requires BOTH: `min_effective_set ≥ k_min`
AND `max_link_prob ≤ p_max`. A single pinned message fails it. Cover transits are
never scored as *targets* (anonymity is only defined for real traffic) but they
DO swell each mix's departure pool — so disabling cover shrinks every real
target's crowd, exactly as in Loopix.

**Why the positive controls fail it, deterministically and robustly.** The
adversary links with each mix's OWN law, so the failures are not statistical
flukes:

- **FIFO / constant-delay mix** (`FifoMix`): every packet's hold is exactly `Δ`,
  so scored with the constant (spike) kernel the posterior lands entirely on the
  one departure at `a* + Δ` — the true one. `p(d*) = 1`, effective set `= 1`, on
  *every* target, on *every* seed, no partition needed. It fails BOTH clauses.
  This is the canonical anonymity-breaking mix, and the harness flags it hard.
- **No-cover mix** (a Poisson mix with the cover process disabled): the hold is
  still memoryless, but at a low real-traffic rate a mix often holds a *single*
  packet, so the causal candidate set is `{d*}` — effective set collapses to 1
  even though `p(d*)` looks unremarkable. It fails clause 1. (Demonstrated by
  `adversary.zig`'s synthetic thin-pool test; the running no-cover control
  confirms clause-1 teeth against the real core, see "Mixing core" below.)

The separation is **1.0 vs ~1/pool, not 0.6 vs 0.4** — there is no seed on which
FIFO "accidentally mixes", so no threshold tuning can make the teeth flaky. The
metric is a pure function of a concrete transcript, itself a pure function of the
netsim seed, so a seed sweep just averages independent draws (LLN). This
robustness is the design's whole point and the reason the harness — not the
mixing core itself — is where the design's weight lies.

## Mixing core

`mixing.zig` holds the three functions the anonymity strategy rests on:

- `sampleExpDelay(prng, mean) Time` — a **memoryless integer** delay draw. Netsim time is integer
  ticks, and a rounded continuous exponential is not memoryless — the discrete memoryless law is the
  **geometric** distribution; this is the one place the anonymity-relevant detail can quietly go wrong.
- `scheduleRelease(prng, cfg, arrival) Time` — the Poisson mix's per-arrival hold/release decision
  (`arrival + sampleExpDelay(_, mean_delay)`).
- `nextCover(prng, cfg) CoverEvent` — the Poisson cover process (exponential inter-arrival + loop/drop choice).

- **Sampling law.** `sampleExpDelay` uses the geometric inverse-CDF
  `hold = ⌊ln(u) / ln(1 − 1/mean)⌋` — constant per-tick release hazard `1/mean`, i.e. genuinely
  memoryless in discrete time. `⌊−mean·ln u⌋` is *also* geometric (with ratio `e^{−1/mean}`) and *is*
  memoryless at tick boundaries — the two differ only at `O(1/mean²)`. The real trap is *rounding*
  (`round`/nearest), which gives the zero bucket half-width and breaks constant hazard near 0. The chosen
  ratio `(1 − 1/mean)` matches the adversary's `e^{−δ/mean}` kernel to `O(1/mean²)`, so the hold pmf is `∝`
  the adversary's likelihood — no departure stands out. A `mean ≤ 1` degenerates to an immediate release.
- **Release by own timer.** Each held packet carries its own scheduled release time and the mix releases by
  that time, not front-first: releasing the oldest arrival on every timer would forward identities in strict
  arrival order whatever the hold law, an order-preserving mix a Kerckhoffs adversary unlinks with
  probability 1 even though the departure times look exponential. The memorylessness test
  (`reorderStats`) pins it.
- **Measurement basis.** Anonymity is scored on a **clean** run (a global *passive* adversary on a
  functioning network — the fault fuzzer is an *active* adversary, out of scope) over the **steady-state**
  window (finite-horizon cool-down excluded; the seed-sweep tests' `measureSteadyState` helper relabels late
  arrivals to cover so they still swell pools but are not scored — `adversary.measure` itself is untouched).
- **The bound.** `AnonymityBound` defaults to `min_effective_set = 2.0`, `max_link_prob = 0.9`, set
  against the real Poisson core's measured behaviour over 50 seeds, each mix scored with its own law (the
  figures are in the `AnonymityBound` doc comment in `types.zig`). The seed-sweep test requires the real
  mix to clear the bound with margin (worst effective set ≥ bound + 0.5, worst link probability ≤ bound −
  0.05), and requires FIFO (every target pinned: set 1, link probability 1) and the no-cover control (set
  near 1) to fail it on both clauses.

## Providers, sender-chosen delays, end to end, n−1

- **Providers with mailboxes** (`LoopixConfig.providers`, `PROVIDER_CFG`,
  `providerScenario`): client `c` sends through and receives at provider
  `c % providers`. The ingress provider forwards to the first layer at once (the
  mixes mix); the egress provider stores the packet in the recipient's mailbox;
  the recipient pulls every `fetch_period` and EVERY answer has exactly
  `fetch_batch` slots, real packets padded with dummies — so what a client
  downloads, and when, says nothing about whether anyone wrote to it. Checked:
  every answer the same length, every due packet delivered to the right mailbox.
- **Sender-chosen delays** (`LoopixConfig.sender_chosen_delays`, `MixHeader.delays`):
  the sender draws each hop's hold and the mix obeys it — Loopix/Nym as deployed
  (stateless mixes). Same law, same anonymity: the per-mix invariant and the
  memorylessness band hold for it over 20 seeds.
- **End-to-end sender anonymity** (`adversary.measureEndToEnd`, `SenderBound`):
  the per-mix posterior composed backward through every layer to a distribution
  over CLIENTS (the GPA sees which client transmitted into the first layer and
  follows packets across links; only the mixes hide the matching). Measured on
  `PROVIDER_CFG`, worst real packet over 20 seeds: Poisson mix 5.78 of 8
  possible senders / 0.286 on the true one; FIFO traced back with probability
  1.00; no cover down to 2.00 senders. Bound `(4.0, 0.5)`.
- **n−1 detection from loop cover** (`Attack`, `Loopix.alarms`): with
  sender-chosen delays a client knows when each of its own loops must be back
  (its hop holds + worst-case links + one fetch period + `loop_slack`); a loop
  past that is lost, and `loop_alarm_lost` losses raise the client's alarm. An
  attacker blocking one middle-layer mix for a third of the run is caught,
  during the attack, on every one of 10 seeds; a clean network raises no alarm
  on 20 seeds; with mix-chosen delays the same attack goes unnoticed (nobody
  can know when a loop is due) — which is the reason Loopix puts the delays in
  the packet.
- **Traffic cost** (`TrafficStats`): real/cover packets sent, delivery,
  end-to-end latency (mean/max), cover overhead per real packet, and the same
  in bytes: every byte the protocol hands a link (`link_bytes`, counted in the
  one `Relay.send` every send goes through — client packets, mix and provider
  forwards, mailbox requests, padded mailbox answers), the answers alone
  (`fetch_bytes`) and `bytes_per_real`, the network's bytes per delivered
  application message, cover and padding included. Bytes are those of the
  modeled `MixHeader` (`wire_len`); a real Sphinx packet is larger by a constant
  factor per packet, which does not change any ratio.
- **Topologies** (`LoopixConfig.topology`, `scenarioFor(cfg)`; paper §3): `stratified` (default), `cascade`
  (one chain, `width` must be 1), `multi_cascade` (`width` independent chains, no link between two chains)
  and `free_route` (every mix linked to every other and to the edge; the route is `layers` DISTINCT mixes
  out of all of them). Node numbering is the same; `routing.pickRoute` picks per topology and
  `isExitMix` says which mixes may hand a packet to a provider (the last layer, or any mix in a free route).
  Measured over 5 seeds with light cover (1 per 100 ticks per client; 8 clients, 2 providers, 9 mixes, 3
  hops): mean per-mix set 38.0 (cascade: each mix carries all the traffic) against 13.3 for the others;
  mean sender set of 8: 7.91 cascade / 7.86 stratified / 7.33 free / 7.07 multi-cascade; worst packet
  6.97 / 5.01 / 1.66 / 2.00; mean leakage ε 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.27 / 0.50 nats — the paper's result that
  multi-cascades and a peer-to-peer net spread traffic thin while stratified keeps a cascade's anonymity
  and scales out. `measureEndToEnd` and `measureReceiver` group passes by (mix, hop): the adversary is
  credited with knowing a pass's position in its route, which a layered net gives away and a free route
  does not (there it is a stronger adversary than the real one, so its anonymity is understated).
- **Mixing strategies** (`LoopixConfig.mix_strategy`; paper §3, "batch-and-reorder"): `poisson` (default),
  `threshold` (a mix releases everything it holds, in a random order, once `threshold` packets are in) and
  `timed` (every `batch_period` ticks). A batch leaves at ONE instant, so the adversary's law is
  `DelayModel.batch`: a packet leaves in the first release at or after its arrival, uniformly among that
  batch (set = batch size, linking probability `1/batch`). Measured: a threshold mix has set exactly `n`
  and link `1/n` on every target (threshold 1 is pinned: the FIFO control again), latency 33 / 56 / 83 /
  137 ticks for n = 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 — the trilemma; a timed batch has no floor (a short period leaves a
  round with one packet: set 1.0), mean set 6.9 / 12.2 / 23.2 and latency 71 / 121 / 222 for period
  20 / 40 / 80; without cover a threshold batch keeps its set but waits for traffic (latency 187 against
  83). The shuffle is `mixing.shuffle` from the seeded stream.
- **Mix-originated cover** (`LoopixConfig.mix_loop_interval`, 0 = off): every mix sends a Poisson stream of
  loops through the network back to itself (route as a client's, destination the mix; the mixes get
  overlay links to the first- and last-hop mixes their loops use). They are `loop_cover` transits that swell
  pools and carry no sender mass (`Origin.from_mix`). A mix watches its own loops as a client does
  (`Loopix.mix_alarms`, `mix_loop_alarm_lost`): known hold bound with sender-chosen delays or timed
  batches, none for mix-chosen holds or threshold batches. Measured (5 seeds): 1386 of 1520 loops back
  (the rest in flight at the horizon), no alarm on a clean network, mean per-mix set 30.9 → 36.2 → 47.6 for
  none / one per 60 / one per 20 ticks; a mix that is blocked (`Attack`) alarms, as do the mixes whose
  loops route through it, all after the attack began.
- **Receiver anonymity and sender–receiver unlinkability** (paper §3 and App. A.2, after the Loopix paper):
  `measureReceiver` composes the posterior FORWARD: a last-hop departure's link names its receiver (a
  client, or with providers every client of that provider uniformly — `LoopixConfig.exitRows`; the
  mailbox pull is padded, so no more is observable), and scores the set `2^H` over clients and the mass on
  the true recipient (`ReceiverBound`). `SenderResult.mean_epsilon` / `max_epsilon` are the third-party
  leakage `ε = ln(Pr[true sender] / Pr[S2])` averaged over the other clients `S2` and over packets
  (`Pr` floored at 1e-12; `UnlinkBound`). Measured, clients on the last layer, 8 clients: Poisson worst
  receiver set 7.47, mass 0.221, mean ε 0.001; FIFO set 1.00, mean ε 18.5; no cover: worst packet ε 23.1.
  Behind providers a FIFO mix is traced to the provider and no further (set 4.00, mass 0.25).
  Cover raises every measure: per-mix mean set 17.9 / 30.9 / 66.0 and worst linking 0.393 / 0.184 /
  0.101 at one cover packet per 40 / 15 / 6 ticks per client.
- **Scale** (`LARGE_CFG`, `largeScenario`): 3 layers × 10 mixes, 120 clients
  behind 10 providers, 160 nodes (the `u8` node id caps a network at 255).

## Known limits

- **Not a network.** No byte crosses a real network; the module is graded as a simulator/analysis library
  against the Loopix authors' own tool (see *Compared with*). The netsim hot loop carries the modeled
  `MixHeader`, not a real onion.
- **No PKI.** Mix keys and epochs are not modeled; routing is a deterministic hash (`pickRoute`).
- **Adversary.** The measured guarantee is against a global passive adversary; the only active attacker
  modelled is one blocking a mix (`Attack`), and a blocking attack is detected only with sender-chosen
  delays — with mix-chosen delays nobody can know when a loop is due.
- **Anonymity metrics.** Per-mix, end-to-end sender, receiver and pairwise sender leakage. Each treats a
  mix's departures independently (a relaxation of the one-to-one matching) and credits the adversary with
  a pass's route position. `measureReceiver` counts, as `fallbacks`, last-hop departures with no observed
  next pass: packets still in flight at the horizon (they cannot be real targets once the window drops
  them); a complete transcript has none.
- **Batch mixes ignore sender-chosen delays** and `mean_delay`; a timed batch's first release is at
  `batch_period`, so releases fall on multiples of it. An arrival on a release tick can land in either
  batch; the adversary assumes the earlier.
- **Mix-chosen holds** remain the `DEFAULT_CFG` variant; `PROVIDER_CFG` is the as-deployed one.

## What is deliberately not done

- **A deployable Loopix node or client.** The module carries no real transport; the owner chose to
  grade it as a simulator and analysis library, not to build a node (the open question of whether a node is
  wanted at all is under *Roadmap*).

## Verification

Offline only. Run `scripts/modtest loopix`; the gate (`gate.fable_core_implemented`) is `true`, so no test
is skipped.

- **Sphinx substrate:** a real onion for a 3-mix route peels hop-by-hop, recovering each hop's
  `(next_hop, delay)`, final hop flagged.
- **Anonymity harness teeth:** synthetic transcripts separate a well-mixed pool (holds the invariant)
  from FIFO order-preservation and cover-starved thin pools (both fail); cover transits enlarge a real
  target's crowd without being scored; ties share the true departure's mass (1/k); a transcript the
  adversary cannot follow is counted, not silently uniform; no real traffic is vacuously anonymous.
- **Positive controls end to end:** `FifoMix` through netsim fails both clauses, including under fuzzed
  faults over a seed sweep; the no-cover control fails the bound under identical measurement.
- **Topologies, strategies, loops, receiver:** wiring link counts per topology; cascade order, one chain per
  packet in a multi-cascade, no repeated mix in a free route; delivery and the per-mix and receiver bounds
  through all three; the paper's comparison pinned (cascade pools 2.5x, stratified beats multi-cascade and
  free route on sender anonymity and leakage); more cover, larger sets; threshold set `n` / link `1/n`,
  threshold 1 and a short timed period fail the bound; latency and set grow with the batch; a batch leaves
  in random order; mix loops come home, raise no false alarm, fill pools, alarm under `Attack`;
  receiver and ε against FIFO and no-cover controls; synthetic transcripts for the batch law, the
  receiver composition, ε and a mix loop's empty sender mass; the hostile-packet fuzz also runs a free route
  with threshold batches and mix loops, and a multi-cascade with timed batches.
- **Real mix:** the Poisson `Loopix` holds `AnonymityBound` across a seed sweep, reorders co-resident
  packets (`reorderStats` near 1/2 where order-preserving mixes score zero).
- **Providers and end to end:** topology and mailbox ownership; every answer the same length and every
  due packet delivered; sender-chosen holds keep the per-mix invariant and stay memoryless; the sender of
  every real packet stays hidden through all layers (FIFO and no-cover are traced back); n−1: a blocked mix
  raises the alarm during the attack, a clean network none, a loop's deadline is exactly its holds plus
  every leg at worst plus one fetch plus the slack; config validation refuses what would overflow the
  header, the casts or the mailboxes; a mix drops a header that does not name it as the current hop.
- **Scale and bytes:** at 160 nodes every due packet is delivered, nothing is malformed, and the per-mix and
  end-to-end bounds hold; the byte count lies between what the transcript proves was sent and every leg of
  every packet, and the mailbox bytes equal the answer lengths.
- **Codec and fuzz:** `MixHeader` round trip and fail-closed decode. `LOOPIX_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]`
  runs the deterministic driver (testkit) over the harnesses `loopix-header` (header decode) and
  `loopix-inject` (hostile packets into the relay handlers: never panic, never mis-deliver); each harness
  has an in-suite reach check and a pinned corpus count.
- **Oracles:** none; the guarantees are invariants with positive controls (class C, see *Anchoring*).
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## Backlog / deferred

None.

## Roadmap

- **A deployable Loopix node/client (real transport):** today the module cannot carry a byte over a network; Nym and Katzenpost can. Needs real transport, a PKI/epoch directory, and the real Sphinx header carrying the sender-chosen delays (the simulator models providers with mailboxes and sender-chosen delays already, with a modeled header). Fits §2 (pure Zig) but overlaps `sphinx`/`noise` work; decide whether it is wanted at all before starting. Project-size: a networked node, a directory service and a wire format.
- **Nym-compatible Sphinx (Curve25519):** interop with the only large deployed network needs its packet format; the repo's `sphinx` is secp256k1. Fits §2. Project-size: a second Sphinx packet family matched byte-for-byte to Nym's, which needs a live or recorded Nym oracle.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** netsim anonymity simulation of Loopix paper; modeled header, not byte-compat with real Loopix/Nym
